angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 855,711 km at 175.71 pc = 0.07 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.6910 +/- 0.0113 mas (same row, RUWE 0.97): 175.71 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.23 +/- 0.08 solar radii from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-62 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract): 855,711 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.11 +/- 0.25 solar masses from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-62 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6230 +/- 80 K from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-62 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-62 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-62.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.304, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-62 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.04 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-62 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.3456, from Maciejewski 2020 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AcA....70..181M/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-62 (pscomppars): age 2.6 Gyr, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/A+A/705/A142/tablea1 (Physical properties study of planet systems), column Prot: 6.65 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

rotationPeriodsCatalogued.source: VizieR J/A+A/705/A142/tablea1 (Physical properties study of planet systems), column Prot: 6.65 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place

projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-62 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 9.3 km/s, from Brown et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017MNRAS.464..810B/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (1.23 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.994. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
